findings.description: _read_all returns {} on OSError, ValueError or KeyError, including a corrupt or temporarily unreadable file. The next save, delete or take_by_refresh then rewrites the file from that empty dict, which silently drops every other live session. Sessions that should still be revoked are lost, and users are logged out. The same masking means sign_out_everywhere and purge_expired see no records during a read failure and report success. A missing file is the only case that should map to empty.
findings.suggestion: Return {} only for FileNotFoundError. Raise StoreError for other OSError and for parse errors, so writers do not overwrite the file with an empty or partial state.
findings.title: Read failures are treated as an empty store, so sessions get wiped

findings.description: take_by_refresh deletes the session before the user check and before _issue. If _issue's save fails with a StoreError, the old session is already gone and no new one exists, so the user is logged out. The same happens when a transient failure occurs between take and save.
findings.suggestion: Handle the failure of _issue after take, for example by restoring the old record on error, or make the rotation a single atomic store operation.
findings.title: Refresh token is consumed before validation and the user lookup is not guarded

findings.description: A StoreError on one delete aborts the loop partway. The remaining expired records are not purged and the caller gets an exception instead of a count. The returned count is also len(expired), not the number actually deleted.
findings.suggestion: Catch StoreError per record as in sign_out_everywhere and count only successful deletes.
findings.title: purge_expired does not tolerate StoreError, unlike sign_out_everywhere

findings.description: When delete raises StoreError, it is only logged and the session stays valid. change_password still returns normally, so the caller believes all sessions ended after a password change even though some tokens, including the refresh token, still work. Only a count is returned, with no indication of failure.
findings.suggestion: After the loop, raise if any revocation failed, or return or raise a failure indicator so change_password cannot report success while sessions remain.
findings.title: Failed revocation is swallowed in sign_out_everywhere and change_password

findings.description: FileSessionStore.get and all read without taking the lock. The memory store also reads without a lock in get. This is combined with the read-modify-write sequences under the lock. Reads are atomic with respect to os.replace, but all() followed by delete in sign_out_everywhere can miss a session saved concurrently, for example a login racing a password change.
findings.suggestion: Take the lock in the read methods. For revocation, make the per-user delete a single atomic store operation.
findings.title: Unlocked reads race with the writer
